title: Israel Marks 1,000 Days Since October 7 — Nationwide Protests Demand State Commission of Inquiry
detail: On July 2, 2026 — 1,000 days since the October 7, 2023 massacre — Israel held nationwide commemorations and protests demanding a full, independent state commission of inquiry. Demonstrators blocked Tel Aviv's Ayalon Highway, gathered outside the homes of coalition lawmakers, and clashed with police outside the Knesset. Freed hostage Rom Braslavski told a memorial ceremony, 'I promise here that I will make October 7 the mission of my life, and I will never forget.' The protests followed a June 27–28 lead-up mobilization in which roughly 1,000 people rallied at Haifa's Horev Center and hundreds gathered again at Tel Aviv's Habima Square. Organizers framed the 1,000-day milestone as a rebuke of the coalition's Kallner inquiry bill, which protesters say is designed to produce a politically controlled — not independent — investigation. A Hebrew University poll (April 26, 2026) found 72% of Israelis favor an independent commission of inquiry into the October 7 failures.

media.caption: Protesters commemorate 1,000 days since the October 7 massacre and demand a state commission of inquiry

title: High Court Voids Netanyahu Lawyer's State Comptroller Appointment, Orders Revote Over Secret-Ballot Violation
detail: On July 2, 2026, Israel's High Court of Justice ordered the Knesset to hold a new vote on Michael Rabello's appointment as State Comptroller — the official legally mandated to audit government conduct on October 7 — after ruling the original vote invalid. The Court found that several Likud lawmakers had photographed their supposedly secret ballots with mobile phones during the vote, violating the requirement for a secret ballot in comptroller elections. The ruling followed petitions filed by opposition and watchdog groups who had objected to Netanyahu appointing his own former personal defense attorney to the oversight post central to October 7 accountability. Some senior coalition figures reportedly floated having Knesset Speaker Amir Ohana delay or avoid the court-ordered revote, while several Likud members called for the ruling to be ignored outright — feeding into the broader institutional standoff between the government and judiciary that has defined Israel's 2026 accountability crisis.

media.caption: High Court orders new vote on Michael Rabello's state comptroller appointment after secret-ballot violation
